result.target_topic: 2024 Process Node Manufacturing Status and Roadmap Changes
result.target_summary: As of the end of 2024, most products were manufactured using the Intel 7 node, while high-volume production of the Intel 4 and Intel 3 nodes was shifted to Ireland. The company canceled the productization of Intel 20A to focus on the improved Intel 18A node, which is expected to enter high-volume production in 2025.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
D050 (2023) details factory operations, ramping new process technologies, and supply chain capacity. D049 (2024) details the status of specific process nodes (Intel 7, 4, 3) and their high-volume manufacturing locations (Arizona, Israel, Ireland). Both focus on the operational execution and status of manufacturing nodes.

Both disclosures discuss capital-intensive manufacturing, facility/equipment distribution, and the transition to advanced lithography (EUV) requiring significant investment. D050 highlights supply chain/minimizing disruptions in 2023, while D052 in 2024 details the EUV transition and capex split (55% facility, 45% equipment) driven by this new technology.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company is on track for volume production of 1-gamma DRAM using EUV lithography in calendar 2025 and has begun volume production of its Micron G9 NAND node.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron disclose the transition to EUV lithography for their next-generation process nodes. Intel shifted high-volume production of its Intel 4 and Intel 3 nodes (its first EUV nodes) to Ireland in 2024 and is preparing Intel 18A for high-volume production in 2025. Similarly, Micron is on track for volume production of its 1-gamma DRAM node using EUV lithography in calendar 2025, following its 2023 introduction of the 1-beta production node.

sentences.text: As of the end of 2024, a significant majority of our products were manufactured using our Intel 7 process node in Arizona and Israel, we successfully ramped our Intel 4 and Intel 3 process nodes as our first EUV lithography nodes and shifted high-volume production of those nodes to Ireland, and we canceled the productization of our Intel 20A process node to focus efforts on the improved version of the node, Intel 18A, that we expect to put into high-volume production in 2025 with our new client family of products code-named Panther Lake.
Our 1-gamma DRAM pilot production using EUV lithography is progressing well, and we are on track for volume production in calendar 2025.

comparisons.peer_topic: DRAM production nodes and future expectations
comparisons.peer_summary: The company shipped its industry's first 1β production node in 2023, produced majority 2024 bits on 1α and 1β nodes, and expects volume shipments of the 1γ node using EUV lithography in 2025.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies detail their manufacturing node status and future roadmap regarding advanced lithography. Intel reports that as of the end of 2024, a significant majority of products were manufactured using Intel 7, while it canceled Intel 20A to focus on Intel 18A for 2025. Micron reports that the majority of its 2024 DRAM bit production was on 1α and 1β nodes and expects volume shipments of its 1γ node (employing EUV) in 2025, highlighting a similar focus on next-generation node volume production.

sentences.text: As of the end of 2024, a significant majority of our products were manufactured using our Intel 7 process node in Arizona and Israel, we successfully ramped our Intel 4 and Intel 3 process nodes as our first EUV lithography nodes and shifted high-volume production of those nodes to Ireland, and we canceled the productization of our Intel 20A process node to focus efforts on the improved version of the node, Intel 18A, that we expect to put into high-volume production in 2025 with our new client family of products code-named Panther Lake.
The majority of our DRAM bit production in 2024 was on leading-edge 1α (1-alpha) and 1ß nodes.
We expect volume shipments in 2025 of our next generation of DRAM, the 1γ (1-gamma) node, which will employ EUV lithography production.

comparisons.peer_topic: Fabless manufacturing strategy and supplier responsibilities
comparisons.peer_summary: The company utilizes a fabless strategy, partnering with suppliers for wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging, while suppliers handle the procurement of most raw materials.
comparisons.comparison: Intel discloses its internal manufacturing capital, including specific process nodes and geographic production shifts (e.g., shifting Intel 4/3 to Ireland). In contrast, NVIDIA discloses a fabless strategy where it outsources all phases of manufacturing (wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, packaging) to suppliers, thereby avoiding the costs and risks of owning manufacturing operations.

sentences.text: As of the end of 2024, a significant majority of our products were manufactured using our Intel 7 process node in Arizona and Israel, we successfully ramped our Intel 4 and Intel 3 process nodes as our first EUV lithography nodes and shifted high-volume production of those nodes to Ireland, and we canceled the productization of our Intel 20A process node to focus efforts on the improved version of the node, Intel 18A, that we expect to put into high-volume production in 2025 with our new client family of products code-named Panther Lake.

We utilize a fabless and contracting manufacturing strategy, whereby we employ and partner with key suppliers for all phases of the manufacturing process, including wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging.

While we may directly procure certain raw materials used in the production of our products, such as memory, substrates, and a variety of components, our suppliers are responsible for procurement of most raw materials used in the production of our products.

comparisons.peer_summary: QCT uses internal fabrication facilities for certain RFFE modules and RF filter products, with front-end processes in Germany and Singapore and back-end assembly and test facilities in China and Singapore.
comparisons.comparison: Intel details its internal manufacturing operations and process nodes, such as shifting high-volume production of Intel 4 and Intel 3 to Ireland. QCT (Qualcomm) discloses that while it primarily uses a fabless model, it uses internal fabrication facilities for certain RFFE modules and RF filter products, with front-end processes in Germany and Singapore and back-end assembly in China and Singapore. Both disclose internal manufacturing capabilities, but for different product lines and geographic locations.

sentences.text: As of the end of 2024, a significant majority of our products were manufactured using our Intel 7 process node in Arizona and Israel, we successfully ramped our Intel 4 and Intel 3 process nodes as our first EUV lithography nodes and shifted high-volume production of those nodes to Ireland, and we canceled the productization of our Intel 20A process node to focus efforts on the improved version of the node, Intel 18A, that we expect to put into high-volume production in 2025 with our new client family of products code-named Panther Lake.
QCT primarily uses internal fabrication facilities to manufacture certain RFFE modules and RF filter products, and our manufacturing operations consist of front-end and back-end processes.

The front-end processes primarily take place at manufacturing facilities located in Germany and Singapore and involve the imprinting of substrate wafers with the structure and circuitry required for the products to function (also known as wafer fabrication).
Our back-end manufacturing facilities are located in China and Singapore.
